packageRules.description: Group all non-major updates by manager — keeps majors as individual PRs for review. Specific rules below (vite, go version, terraform) override per Renovate's last-rule-wins semantics.
Flag major version bumps for human review (audit finding I-7). automerge is already false by default; the label surfaces majors on the dashboard.
Pin PostGIS to PostgreSQL v17 - major version bumps require database migration
Pin Go to 1.26.x across all managers (Go modules, GitHub Actions, Docker)
Pin @vitejs/plugin-react to v5 until Babel → @rolldown/plugin-babel migration
Group Vite ecosystem so peer-dep-coupled major bumps land in one PR
Group all Terraform updates into one PR

Keep every uv pin in one PR. The Dockerfile tag and pyproject.toml's [tool.uv] required-version must move together — uv.lock carries a format revision, so a uv newer than the image's can write a lock the production build can't read. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule above to win under last-rule-wins.

Keep CPython in one PR across .python-version (pyenv manager) and the stravapipe Dockerfile's `uv python install` (custom manager below), and hold it at 3.14.x — pants `interpreter_constraints` (>=3.14,<3.15) and pyproject `requires-python` forbid 3.15. Without the custom manager the Dockerfile line drifted behind .python-version. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule to win under last-rule-wins.

Keep every Flyway pin in one PR. The schemas/database/Dockerfile tag and the `docker run` tag in ci.yml's migration step must move together, and both must stay in step with the deploy repo's flyway-migrate action — a migration verified in CI by one Flyway version but applied to prod by another is the drift the pin exists to prevent. Must stay after the group-by-manager rule to win under last-rule-wins.

customManagers.description: Track [tool.uv] required-version as the uv image, so it bumps alongside the Dockerfile tag rather than drifting silently.

Track the CPython patch the stravapipe Dockerfile installs via `uv python install X.Y.Z` — a raw shell command no built-in manager sees, which is why it drifted behind .python-version (3.14.5 vs 3.14.6). The `python version` packageRule above groups it with the pyenv bump and caps it at 3.14.x.

Track the Flyway image the CI migration step runs via `docker run flyway/flyway:X` — a raw shell command the github-actions manager does not parse, so without this the tag would silently rot at whatever was pinned. The schemas/database/Dockerfile FROM is covered by the dockerfile manager; the `flyway` packageRule above keeps both in one PR.
